page.layout: One printed page of running text in a single column; the right and left edges carry cut-off fragments of text from the neighbouring page, which are not transcribed. Running head at the top with page number 230 at left.

main_text.l: Conf. pag. 524. quia de usu & fine
agitur quid profit Sacramentum) esse Sacramenta
Dei erga nos, per quæ movet Deus corda ad
vinum ponitur, in cibum & alimoniam nobis,
non esse, quod offertur: quando comedere
operari nobiscum ut una fiat substantia. Quando
denique pro nobis dari dicitur, non
potius, quam suum esse, quod ag-
itur. Christus. Et hunc finem tradit
23 Est & alter finis, quem proponit Apostolus 1. Cor. 11. v.
Apostolus, ut tertiâ vice ordine eundem
repetat. Hæc commemoratio, ut ordinata est,
ad finem principalem: ita habet conjunctionem.

page.notes: Right and left edges are heavily damaged and show-through from the facing page; several words at the edges are illegible and the marginal text on the right edge is cut off. Several words in the body are partly obscured by stains and are uncertain, notably "Christus", "quod agitur" and "Apostolus" near the edges; the transcription of the lower paragraph is approximate.
